claims.text: The starting MoNbTaTiW alloy is a solid solution.
The starting alloy contains at least five elements at concentrations of at least 5 atomic percent each.
The intervention introduces boron at 5 atomic percent into MoNbTaTiW.
Introducing boron produces a MoNbTaTiWB alloy.
The comparison alloys will be fabricated by spark plasma sintering, annealed at 1200 °C for 2 hours, and furnace cooled.
Adding 5 atomic percent boron will alter the alloy's electron-phonon coupling.
Adding 5 atomic percent boron will alter the alloy's lattice dynamics.
The boron-induced changes in electron-phonon coupling and lattice dynamics will increase the phonon-mediated pairing interaction.
Increasing the phonon-mediated pairing interaction will enhance superconductivity by increasing the critical temperature.
MoNbTaTiWB will have a superconducting critical temperature at least 0.5 K higher than that of baseline MoNbTaTiW.
The proposed alloy is applicable only if it remains a solid solution with at least five elements present at no less than 5 atomic percent each.
Failure of boron addition to significantly change both lattice dynamics and electron-phonon coupling would falsify the proposed mechanism.
